title: Rulekeeper rule
description: Authoring schema for one Rulekeeper rule file: one YAML file declares one rule, and the rule's identity is its filename stem (the basename without the .yaml or .yml extension), never a field in the document. Required: version, files, scope and check. Optional: filter, decision, settings and enabled. This document exists so an editor can complete and check the declarative shape; the compiler stays the source of truth. It cannot express what the runtime checks semantically, such as the non-executable JSONPath subset, the native ast-grep rule DSL, glob grammar, duplicate YAML keys or whether a regex-kind check.rule is a syntactically valid JavaScript regular expression, and it is deliberately stricter than the runtime about unknown properties: here an unknown property is an error so typos are visible, while the runtime warns about it and ignores it.

version.description: Rule format version. Exactly the string "v1" (quote it in YAML so it is not read as a number); a missing value, the numeric 1 or any other version fails to compile.

enabled.description: Whether the rule takes part in check. A disabled rule is still loaded, compiled and validated, but it is skipped before file selection, so it produces no result and no decision-provider access. An actual boolean is required: "false" as a string is not disabled.

nonBlankString.description: A string containing at least one non-whitespace character.

glob.description: A non-empty glob matched with Node's path.matchesGlob against the logical, working-root-relative filepath (the check working directory, or the folder inspect was given). Supports *, ?, [...], brace expansion and extglob; ** spans directory levels including zero, while * stops at a separator, and wildcards do not match dot-prefixed segments.

changed.description: Revision selection for this scope. true (the default) decides only scopes that differ between the reviewed base and head; false reviews every selected scope of the head. It is ignored for whole-file inputs, and a grouped rule reads the current tree instead of a diff either way.

files.title: File selection
files.description: Which filepaths the rule applies to. A file is selected when it matches included and matches no excluded glob; an excluded file is skipped before its source is read.

included.description: At least one glob; a filepath must match one of them to be selected.

excluded.description: Optional globs subtracted after inclusion. Omit it, or leave it empty, to exclude nothing.

exampleList.description: Snippets kept exactly as written, including indentation and newlines. Each entry must contain a non-whitespace character. An omitted category is the same as an empty one.

examples.title: Contrastive examples
examples.description: Optional representative snippets for the policy: a good snippet satisfies the rule, a bad one violates it. They are never parsed, executed, scored, or used to filter scopes; YAML comments inside a snippet may explain why it is good or bad. Only when at least one snippet exists in either list does an AI check carry them verbatim to the decision provider — a good snippet under instructions.examples.good, a bad one under instructions.examples.bad, with the empty counterpart list kept; a rule whose examples are absent or both empty omits instructions.examples entirely. Prefer pairs that differ in the one fact the policy turns on.

check.title: Check
check.description: Required. How a matched scope is judged. kind selects the evaluator: AI consults the decision provider, regex tests the scope locally with no provider access. rule is the policy or the pattern, and examples and violation-message are the optional contrastive snippets and reporting metadata that accompany it.

kind.description: Which evaluator runs, and the spelling is exact: ai, Regex or any other casing is an unknown value. AI (the default) sends rule as instructions.rule, the fixed question as instructions.question, and its good and bad examples as instructions.examples to the decision provider — but only when at least one example exists, since a rule with none omits instructions.examples entirely. regex treats rule as raw JavaScript regular-expression source and tests it locally against the scope's string data, or against the selected scope source when the scope carries no scalar data; a match follows the rule and a mismatch is a violation, with no API key or backend involved.

rule.description: For kind AI, the policy statement a matched context is expected to satisfy, stated declaratively as the requirement itself and not as an evaluator workflow or a command sequence; it is carried verbatim to the decision provider. For kind regex, the raw JavaScript regular-expression source applied to the scope, written without delimiters and with no separate flags field; the runtime compiles and validates it, and this schema cannot express whether it is a valid pattern. Either way this is the check-level rule, a different field from the nested scope.rule, which is the native ast-grep structural selector.
examples: Memory limit must be less than or equal to memory request * 1.5.

violation-message.description: Optional short human-readable explanation printed beside each violation. Static reporting metadata: it is never generated by the model and is not sent to the decision provider.
examples: Memory limit must not exceed 1.5 times the memory request.

filter.title: Applicability filter
filter.description: Optional predicate over a selected scope that decides relevance, not compliance: a scope that passes is still reviewed, and valid code still reaches the decision provider. A mapping carries exactly one operator, and groups may nest.

oneOf.title: non_empty
oneOf.description: True when the JSONPath selects at least one value that is present and not null, an empty string, an empty array or an empty object. 0, false and whitespace-only strings count as present.

non_empty.description: A JSONPath starting with $, evaluated over the scope wrapper { id, source, data?, captures?, lines? } and not over the file, the diff or the context. Non-executable selection only: script expressions and predicate expressions are rejected rather than evaluated. $.data.tags tests the array itself while $.data.tags[*] tests its elements, and a path that selects nothing is not non-empty. Filter fields live under $.data and $.captures; the raw file root is not part of the scope.

all.description: A non-empty sequence of filters; an empty sequence is rejected.

oneOf.title: any
oneOf.description: At least one child filter must pass.

any.description: A non-empty sequence of filters; an empty sequence is rejected.

not.description: The single child filter to negate.

decision.title: Decision grouping
decision.description: Optional choice of what one review call judges. Omitted, every selected scope is decided on its own. file, folder and project decide one group at a time and read the current working tree, ignoring the diff entirely. Choose the smallest grouping that answers the policy.

group_by.description: scope decides each selected scope on its own; file judges one file's selected scopes together; folder judges one directory's; project judges the whole selected tree. A grouped decision sends the group's member files and scopes to the provider as one consolidated request.

level.description: Only for group_by: folder. 0 (the default) is the file's own directory, -1 its parent, -2 the grandparent, and so on; an ancestor above the working root clamps to '.'. Must be a non-positive integer within the safe integer range, and it is meaningless for the other groupings.

settings.title: Per-rule decision settings
settings.description: Optional overrides of the environment decision defaults, for this rule alone. An explicit check --threshold still wins over a rule threshold. The API key and base URL have no per-rule setting and stay environment-only.

model.description: Decision model name sent to the backend. Falls back to the configured environment model. Set it only when this rule justifies a different model.

threshold.description: Probability above which a decision counts as following the rule, inclusive of 0 and 1. A real number only: a quoted decimal is rejected. A decision exactly at the threshold does not follow the rule. Precedence is an explicit check --threshold, then this, then RK_THRESHOLD, then 0.4.

backend.description: Decision backend. The Jev backend is the only one that exists, so this value is always jev; any other name is rejected offline rather than silently ignored.

scope.title: Scope selection
scope.description: Required. format names the registered plugin that turns a matching file into scopes. The builtin formats are yaml, protobuf and ast-grep; a host may register more, and those formats' options are not known to this schema.

scopeYaml.title: yaml scope
scopeYaml.description: Parses each YAML document in the file and selects one scope per node the path chooses, including merged and aliased content. Every document is parsed, so a malformed document fails the match instead of looking empty.

path.description: Non-executable JSONPath over the parsed document. $ selects the whole document; one level of $.key descends one mapping level, while $..key searches at any depth, so spelling and depth both matter. Selecting a node that holds a mapping gives that mapping as the scope data.

key.description: Optional non-executable JSONPath relative to each selected node that resolves to exactly one string or number, which then names the scope: the scope id becomes `${documentIndex}:${keyValue}` instead of a pointer. Useful to keep an identity stable when a mapping is reordered.

scopeProtobuf.title: protobuf scope
scopeProtobuf.description: Reads protobuf RPC declarations and their HTTP annotations structurally, not as a compiler: no imports, type resolution or descriptor validation. RPC records expose { id, package, service, name, http: { bindings: [{ method, url }] } }. Select an HTTP subtree node to send only that node's value, such as a binding object or a URL string. Unannotated RPCs have empty bindings.

path.description: Non-executable JSONPath over { rpcs: [...] }. Select an RPC record, its http object, bindings array, binding object, or method/url string. $.rpcs[*].http.bindings[*].url judges each URL separately; use $.rpcs[*].http.bindings[*] when the method also matters. Scope data is exactly the selected value, with its source location. Other nodes, such as RPC names or the rpcs array, fail at match time.

scopeAstGrep.title: ast-grep scope
scopeAstGrep.description: Selects syntax nodes with the native @ast-grep/napi engine. One scope is one matched node; scope.data is absent and scope.captures carries the $NAME and $$$NAME captures the selector binds. Matching is syntactic, with no type or dataflow verification.

language.description: The language of the reviewed files. Names are case-insensitive and the catalog covers 31 languages, including the napi builtins (css, html, javascript, tsx, typescript) and the packaged grammars (for example go, python, java, rust, csharp, glimmer-javascript); conventional aliases such as js, ts, py, rb and golang also work. A host may register more languages, and an unknown name reaches the native parser as written, which fails when the grammar is unavailable. Note that this is the language of the source files, not the spelling of the file extension.

rule.description: The native ast-grep structural selector: the query that picks nodes, written in the ast-grep rule DSL (kind, pattern, has, any, all, not, inside and so on), with metavariables such as $SLICE and $$$ARGS. This is a different field from the top-level policy rule. Its syntax is checked by the native parser when the rule compiles, and this schema deliberately does not constrain it; a misspelled metavariable or an unavailable language surfaces at runtime.

constraints.description: Optional native ast-grep constraints mapping that narrows metavariable matches, for example restricting $SLICE by regex or kind.

utils.description: Optional native ast-grep utils mapping of reusable named sub-rules referenced from the selector.

scopeCustom.title: custom scope format
scopeCustom.description: A scope format registered by the host in addition to the builtins. The plugin receives every key except format and changed and validates its own options, so this branch accepts arbitrary option keys and cannot check them here.

format.description: The format name of a host-registered scope plugin, for example kv or whole-file. An unknown format fails at load time, and rule YAML can never name code to import.
